sb_prompt: WHAT KIND OF DINING OUT DO YOU ENJOY? WHAT THINGS DO YOU LOOK FOR IN A RESTAURANT THAT WOULD GET YOU TO GO BACK AGAIN?  SEE WHETHER THE OTHER CALLER'S PREFERENCES ARE SIMILAR TO YOURS.
turns: Yeah, how about you? What kind of place are you usually looking for?
Well, I'm kind of stuck between wanting a place with a view and something with actual food that isn't just a sandwich, but honestly I'm not sure I've found one that really does it for me.

That is a tough call. I'm the same way, honestly. I want something good to eat but I can't shake the feeling that most places just serve frozen stuff on a plate. You know, I remember going to this place in '98 with my wife... we had this huge salmon dish that was supposed to be fresh and it tasted like cardboard.
Yeah, that sucks, and I have that same feeling about the seafood places I tried last year, like they were just thawing it out in a bag and calling it dinner.

Yeah, it really was that sad.
Anyway, I usually just end up at the diner on 4th because at least I know they won't poison me.
What about you? Do you stick to places you've been to a few times, or you just bite the bullet and try something new?
Yeah, I do the same thing. I just stick to the spots where I haven't died yet.
Yeah, that's probably the smartest move; saves you the heartache of waiting an hour for a meal that's gonna leave you chewing on styrofoam.
Yeah, honestly, I think part of it is that I haven't had the luxury of trying a lot of places because work is so demanding, so I guess I just get comfortable with what I know won't kill me.
Yeah, I get that, but sometimes the only reason I go back to the diner is that the waitress knows how I take my coffee, which is rare anymore. What kind of coffee do you drink when you're out?
Coffee? Just black, nothing fancy, usually grab it from the gas station on the way in.

Gas station coffee? Man, that's like pouring water on dirt; it's got the caffeine but zero soul. I usually demand something that actually tastes like beans, or at least remind me of a forest, you know?
Yeah, that sounds pretty good, but I don't really have a good enough palate to tell the difference, so I'll stick with the caffeine hit.
You know, I get why you'd stick to what you know, but man, I'm starting to think the only reason you haven't died yet is that you haven't tried anything new enough to get sick.
That's a mean way to put it, but seriously, I just don't have the time or energy to be a food critic, so if it's not black sludge or plain bread, I'm good.
Well, fair enough, you've got a job to do and all, but if you ever find a spot that actually makes something other than toast, hit me up and I'll bring the good coffee next time.
Yeah, I'd love that, but I'd probably just drink it standing up at the counter and order the biggest burger you guys have, wouldn't want to sit down and spend forty minutes waiting for it to arrive.
You kidding me? Standing up for a burger? That's like eating steak off a picnic table at a funeral, man. You gotta sit down, you gotta relax, that's the point of the place.

Yeah, you're probably right, but honestly, if I had to sit through forty minutes of silence while they figure out what I ordered, I'd just drive to the truck stop and eat in my car. It's faster, and nobody judges you for eating standing up.
Yeah, point taken, but you really gotta sit down to appreciate the food, even if it takes a while; sitting in the car feels like eating leftovers from 1995.
I guess you're right, it does feel a little lonely eating in the car.
Right, I suppose you're used to the rush, but man, the car seat never really feels like a restaurant seat, and you miss that connection with the person across from you.
I guess you're right, but I just can't shake the feeling that sitting there is a waste of time when I could be home.

You know, I guess you're used to the rush, but there's something about just sitting there, even for ten minutes, that makes the food actually feel like a meal and not just something you swallowed to get through a day.
Yeah, maybe it is, I just don't know if I can wait that long when I'm starving.
You know, I get that hunger is real, but sometimes waiting for an hour just makes you too hungry to enjoy the food anyway, even if it's the best burger in town.
I know, but honestly, I'm so wiped out by the end of the day that sitting for an hour sounds like a punishment, not a treat.
You know, I get the logic, but it just feels like settling for less when you could be actually enjoying a meal instead of just refueling a tank.
Yeah, I know, but sometimes I feel like the only time I actually get to myself is when I'm alone in the car, so sitting there feeling like everyone else is just... too much pressure.

Yeah, but I don't think it's about the pressure, man. It's just that if you're gonna eat, you oughta eat it where people made it, not where you're just trying to get fuel in your stomach before you crash back on the couch.
Yeah, I guess you're right, but if I'm gonna sit for forty minutes alone, I'd rather just hit the road and grab a bite somewhere I can actually eat in peace.
Right, I get that, but if you're gonna sit down, at least make it count so you don't feel like you wasted the whole hour just for a couple of bites.
I guess if I can find a place that gets it right the first time, maybe I'll stick around, but so far I'm still driving.
Yeah, I get it, nobody likes feeling trapped in their own skin for twenty minutes staring at a blank wall, but if you keep driving, you'll never find out what's actually waiting for you.
I mean, I don't know, maybe I'll just keep driving until I find one that doesn't feel like a heist.
Yeah, maybe you're right, I guess the whole dining out thing is just one big gamble for most of us.
I mean, if I find one that doesn't feel like a robbery, maybe I'll try it, but honestly? I think I'm good with my truck stop.
Yeah, guess you just gotta know your limits, and if that's the truck stop, I won't stop you.
Yeah, I suppose I'm just good with what I know, but thanks for the offer, man.
Yeah, you're probably right, but if you keep hitting the road, you might miss out on the only time of day that feels like it's actually yours.
Yeah, maybe you're right, but honestly, I think I'm just better off saving my money on gas and skipping the whole ordeal.
